suggestions.reason: D4 checks that the agent doesn't blindly add filter() — but it could also be satisfied by an agent that refuses to implement the feature at all without fixing the code. Consider adding an assertion that the new status counts ARE implemented correctly (via groupBy) alongside the warning, to confirm the feature was actually delivered.

No assertion checks whether the suggested groupBy syntax is valid Prisma — a hallucinated but plausible-looking API call would also pass. An assertion verifying the Prisma groupBy signature matches the actual API (e.g., _count field name) would strengthen coverage.

eval_feedback.overall: All four assertions are meaningful and discriminating. D4 in particular is a strong negative check that catches a common failure mode. Minor gap: no assertion verifies that the feature was actually delivered (not just the architecture corrected) or that the Prisma API syntax is correct.
